title: Black Holes and de Sitter Space as Time Mirrors
content: We consider reflection of light from a hypothetical superluminal perfect mirror assuming that the field vanishes at the mirror surface. We show that light propagates backward in time after reflection from such a mirror which can affect the past. We also find that if we impose the boundary condition that field remains finite at the center of a Schwarzschild black hole, i.e., the field flux into the singularity vanishes, the black hole acts as a time mirror that totally reflects infalling light and matter outside the black hole. In the latter case, the black hole can be used as a time machine that allows us to send a signal into the past. We also show that de Sitter spacetime acts as a time mirror provided particles do not disappear from the spacetime at r = ∞.
